documents.title: Hematology Follow-up
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
HEMATOLOGY & ONCOLOGY - FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 07/08/2024
Patient: Gregory Kearney, DOB 11/11/1975

Mr. Kearney is 48 and was seen here in 2022 for folate deficiency anemia. He called to come back on his own because he has kept getting sick with infections over the past several months, bruises easily, and has lost about 10 kg over six months without trying. Splenectomy after a car accident roughly a decade ago. He admits he rarely takes his penicillin.

Meds as reported: folic acid 1 mg daily, thiamine 100 mg daily, cholecalciferol 2000 units daily, penicillin VK 250 mg twice daily (rarely taken), hydroxychloroquine 200 mg twice weekly (never started).
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: heavy daily alcohol use continues.

Exam: afebrile. Pale. Multiple ecchymoses of varying age on the arms and legs. Abdomen soft and unremarkable, no hepatosplenomegaly. No lymphadenopathy.

Labs: Hgb 9.8 g/dL, MCV 92 fL, WBC 3.2, platelets 120. Peripheral smear: Howell-Jolly bodies.

Assessment:
1. Asplenia with overwhelming post-splenectomy infection risk, heightened by alcohol use, cirrhosis, malnutrition, low white count and non-adherence to prophylaxis.
2. Anemia with leukopenia and mild thrombocytopenia in the setting of alcohol use and cirrhosis; the smear changes are those of asplenia.

Plan:
- Long discussion about OPSI: fever or shaking chills means same-day emergency care, not waiting it out.
- Take penicillin VK 250 mg twice daily every day.
- Keep post-splenectomy vaccines current with his PCP; a pneumococcal update is due.
- Continue folic acid and thiamine.
- PCP to follow counts; we are available as needed.

Hematology & Oncology

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: First visit here in almost a year (missed February, cancelled May). Hematology letter from 7/8 reviewed: OPSI risk, Howell-Jolly bodies, counts down. He went to them himself after a rough winter and spring of being sick on and off. He never came here for those. Lost weight, pants falling off. Drinking daily. Taking folic acid and D3 most days. Penicillin: he has the bottle, 'trying.'
O: weight 53 kg. Thin with muscle wasting. Several bruises on the forearms and shins. No jaundice, no ascites. Lungs clear.
A/P:
1. Asplenia with OPSI risk, per hematology. PCV20 today as they suggested; MenACWY was boosted 2023. Penicillin VK re-sent, same dose. Went over the fever plan again, wrote it on a card for his wallet: fever or chills, call us and go to the ED.
2. Severe malnutrition: weight now 53 kg. Same food plan; he says money is tight. Gave the list of local food pantries.
3. Folate deficiency anemia, cytopenias: counts as per hematology; CBC next visit.
4. Cirrhosis, hep C: CMP, INR today.
5. AUD severe: AUDIT-C 12. Declined referral.
RTC 3 months, I'd like to see him more often.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL EXAM
Lives alone in his rental. Working construction and grounds through the fall. Drinking every day, roughly a bottle. Former wife still checks on him now and then. PHQ-9 6: tired, sleeps badly, not hopeless, no thoughts of self-harm.
Meds: folic acid, thiamine, D3 daily; penicillin VK on and off; hydroxychloroquine never started.
ROS: no fevers, no chest pain, no breathlessness, no belly swelling, no black stools, no vomiting blood, no confusion.
Exam: thin, weight steady around 55 kg. HEENT normal. Heart regular, no murmur today. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, midline scar, no ascites. Hands with scarring and darker patches. No edema. Fine tremor, gait steady.
Health maintenance: FIT negative July. Asplenia vaccines: PCV20 2024, MenACWY 2023 (next 2028), MenB and Hib done. Hep A/B series done. Tdap 2018. Flu and COVID at the October nurse visit.
A/P: problems unchanged. Labs today incl. vitamin D and PTH. Same counseling. RTC 4 months.

documents.body: Liver tests and INR about his usual. Platelets and white count mildly low as before. Hemoglobin in the 11s. Vitamin D 26, PTH still a touch high. Keep D3 2000 daily. Portal message sent.

documents.title: Psychiatry Consultation
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - CONSULTATION-LIAISON PSYCHIATRY
Date of service: 07/21/2026
Patient: Gregory Kearney, DOB 11/11/1975
Requested by: medicine team
Reason: acute confusion and agitation

HPI: 50-year-old man admitted 3 days ago with acute pancreatitis. Background of severe alcohol use disorder, alcoholic cirrhosis, chronic hepatitis C, asplenia, porphyria cutanea tarda and nutritional deficiencies. Over the last day nursing found him more and more restless and irritable. This morning his former wife, visiting, found him confused and shaking and called the nurse. He is now seeing snakes on the floor of the room. She gives a history of about 25 years of heavy daily drinking; he has had nothing to drink since he came in.

Meds prior to admission: folic acid, thiamine, cholecalciferol, penicillin VK (inconsistent); hydroxychloroquine prescribed, never taken.
Allergies: NKDA.

Vitals at time of consult: T 38.2 C, BP 162/98, HR 126, RR 24.

Mental status: disoriented to time and place, oriented to self. Frightened, hypervigilant, pulling at his IV lines. Visual hallucinations. Diaphoretic with fine tremor of the hands. Heart and lungs otherwise unremarkable; neurologic exam otherwise nonfocal.

Assessment: alcohol withdrawal delirium, onset roughly 72 hours after his last drink.

Recommendations:
1. Symptom-triggered withdrawal treatment per the primary team's protocol, with close monitoring.
2. One-to-one sitter; frequent reorientation, lights on by day and dim at night, family at bedside when possible.
3. Continue thiamine supplementation.
4. Avoid restraints if at all possible.
5. Addiction medicine follow-up after discharge; he will need a plan for his drinking.
We will follow.

Consultation-Liaison Psychiatry

documents.title: ICU Transfer Note
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - MEDICAL ICU TRANSFER / ADMISSION NOTE
Date of service: 07/21/2026
Patient: Gregory Kearney, DOB 11/11/1975

Reason for ICU: hypoxemic respiratory failure.

HPI: 50-year-old man with severe alcohol use disorder, alcoholic cirrhosis, asplenia, porphyria cutanea tarda and malnutrition, admitted from our ED on 7/18 with acute pancreatitis after two days of severe epigastric pain boring into his back and repeated vomiting, taking little by mouth. On hospital day 3 he developed alcohol withdrawal delirium (psychiatry seen this morning) and this afternoon became acutely short of breath on the floor. He was put on supplemental oxygen with little change in his saturation. He was transferred to the ICU.

Allergies: NKDA.

Vitals on transfer: T 38.3 C, HR 112, RR 32, BP 100/62, SpO2 83% on room air.

Exam: tachypneic and in visible distress, using accessory muscles. Diffuse bilateral crackles. Heart tachycardic, regular. Abdomen with epigastric tenderness and guarding.

Data: glucose 236 mg/dL (elevated). Calcium 7.1 mg/dL (low). ABG on FiO2 0.60: PaO2 55 mmHg. Portable chest x-ray: bilateral patchy opacities. Bedside echo: normal LV function, no pericardial effusion. ECG: no acute changes.

Course in the first hours: aggressive IV fluid resuscitation and supportive care continued; oxygenation did not improve and he was intubated and placed on mechanical ventilation.

Assessment:
1. Acute respiratory distress syndrome with refractory hypoxemia. With normal LV function, no effusion and an unremarkable ECG, a cardiac cause is excluded; this is lung injury from his systemic illness, the acute pancreatitis.
2. Acute alcoholic pancreatitis.
3. Alcohol withdrawal delirium.
4. Asplenia, cirrhosis, malnutrition.

Plan: lung-protective ventilation, supportive care for pancreatitis, withdrawal management with psychiatry following, nutrition consult.

Medical Intensive Care Unit
